items.title: Panama Francis interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 1, 1995
items.q: he used to hire the musicians for Louis, so he had hired Sid Catlett to play with Roy.

ctx.x: Let me ask you, how did you get the nickname “Panama?”

I’ve been asked that so many times. I wish I had a dollar for every time I’ve been asked that. What happened, I joined Roy Eldridge. In fact I met Roy at a jam session, ‘cause as I say I was very competitive and I used to go looking for jam sessions. And so I went to this jam session and Roy Eldridge heard me. And he liked the way that I played behind him. And his drummer was leaving the band to join Chic Webb’s band because Chic was in the hospital. He hadn’t died yet but he left to join Chic’s band. And so Roy…

Glaser walks in. And he asked for Big Sid. So Roy said “I don’t know where he is.” So he said “well who is that setting up the drums there?” And without batting an eye, he just turned around and said “oh, that’s Panama” ‘cause I had on a Panama hat. It was the summertime and I had just come from Florida, and that was the style in Florida, a Panama hat. So I had on a Panama hat. And I was too scared to tell the fellows, you know here I am in the big league now. Too scared to tell the guys that my name was David.…

items.title: 61521_David Albert Francis oral history interview
items.q: And, later on, when I came to New York, whenever he was in town, we used to hang out together every now and then

ctx.x: Well, [he'd ask me] different things about the drums, and he was trying to play -- and things I would see him do, I would ask about them, and he tried to explain them to me.

And, later on, when I came to New York, whenever he was in town, we used to hang out together every now and then, and I will never forget the time that I was out in California, and he had his own group at a club there, I think the club was called The Last Word, that was where I first saw Allen Eager -- Allen Eager was playing out there at the time.

And Sid and I used to hang out there, because at that time, he was doing very well for himself; I mean, as a leader. Then I got the pleasure of being with him again in at Wildwood, New Jersey when he was with Louis Armstrong. Louis Armstrong had Jack Teagarden T.
